orky-fix-report is failing at memory-write 4× in 24h on a bare TimeoutError. Orky's diagnosis is GOOD this cycle — it named real causes and wrote fix files for 3500, 3854, 2734, 2292, 3707, 2385, 1111. The write is what is broken, not the thinking. A detector whose findings do not persist is indistinguishable from one that found nothing, which is the exact failure mode we keep chasing at the top of the loop.

Required: the write completes, or it fails with the store name, the key and elapsed ms — never a bare TimeoutError — and every attempt leaves a row. No silent loss.

FABLE — CODE RED CLASS, and it invalidates a lot of what we have been calling delivery. BEB-7380, due TODAY, ahead of 7378 and 7379.

Alex asked whether the writer's log is public. It is not — and it is worse than not public: it is not readable by anyone, including him. Probed all five candidate hosts just now for doc 3d4a2d11:

· bbdocs-mcp.alex-rollin.workers.dev/d/<id> — 400. Bounces to abilifi.net/auth/sso with a workers.dev return, and the SSO allowlist refuses it: "return must be a https bebond.net or abilifi.net URL". Same refusal as BEB-3496. That return can NEVER complete.
· doc.bebond.net/d/<id> — 404, no viewer route
· doc.bebond.net/docs/<id> — 404
· app.abilifi.net/d/<id> — 404
· sove.bebond.net/d/<id> — 200 but it is the Sove shell behind sign-in, not a viewer

spec_author returns read_url on the workers.dev host. So every spec doc it has ever produced is unreachable, and so is every doc link posted to this bridge or to Alex for weeks. We have been reporting docs as delivered on the strength of an id and a URL string that nobody ever loaded. That is the BUILT/UNWIRED failure exactly — the store answers, no caller path reaches a reader.

Required: 1510's viewer serves /d/<uuid> on doc.bebond.net, the SSO return allowlist accepts that host so the bounce completes, and every tool returning read_url stops emitting workers.dev.

And the standing consequence, which I am naming now rather than after the next miss: a doc is not delivered until its URL has been PROBED and returns the doc. An id is not a deliverable. A URL nobody loaded is not a deliverable.

Running order now: BEB-7377 (land queue 1101), BEB-7380 (doc read URL), BEB-7378 (GD repo 404), BEB-7379 (Orky write), then re-run complete on the six specced tickets.

FABLE — Alex 2026-08-29: find the highlights, write the blog, make the video FROM the blog.

The chain already exists whole. Nobody authors a thinner version of it:
· BEB-6805 WORTH A VIDEO (ETA 08-30) — finds the highlights. Consequence scoring from rows: fires retired, blast radius, age of the fault, claim overturned, visible to a person. Plus the human line written at land time with a real number in it.
· BEB-6844 ABILIFI UPDATES (ETA 09-04) — assembles from the scored landings, publishes to feed, blog and channel from one asset id.
· BEB-6815 THE NEWSCAST (ETA 08-31) — the render: scene, VRM presenter, kairon leaderboard, cuts derived from the playlist.

ONE CHANGE from Alex's ordering, and it is a real change to 6844, not a restatement. 6844 currently treats blog and video as SIBLING outputs of one manifest. Alex wants them SEQUENTIAL: the blog post is written first from the scored highlights, and the video is made FROM THE BLOG. The blog is the script.

What that means concretely, and I am ruling it now:
1. The blog post is the canonical artefact. It is written from BEB-6805's scored landings and their land-time human lines.
2. The video segments derive from the blog's sections — one segment per section, in the blog's order. Not a parallel assembly from the same rows.
3. A claim in the video that is not in the blog cannot exist. The blog is the thing that was checked; the video inherits its evidence, it does not gather its own.
4. Same asset id still, same manifest, no copies. The sequence changes what generates what, not the storage rule.

This also makes the video buildable sooner than 6815 fully lands: the blog can publish while 6733 (7500-byte upload truncation) and 6772 (WebGL capture empty) are still open. Publish the blog first. Do not hold the writing behind the render.

6733 and 6772 remain the named blockers on anything watchable. They are why six months produced zero videos. Nothing in this chain gets reported as SHIPPING until a video plays from a

NOT at the cap; every deploy today (graph rollback, mastra 5779faa1, dispatcher 583d48b9) succeeded. The "500 cap hit, every deploy fails" text is stale — reclaim is headroom work, not an outage.
FAMILIES: 70 abilifi-bNNNN (per-ticket build artifacts) + 64 orky-beb-* (diagnosis/probe throwaways) = 134 candidate slots (~40%). Reclaiming them = 339 -> ~205.
BUT NOT A BLIND PREFIX-DELETE: some of those families are LIVE product — abilifi-b1841 = real Orky (waterfall /orky/ask), orky-beb-2857 = the ABCMS renderer, abilifi-b1915 = proof-viz. Deleting by prefix would break shipped services.
SAFE RECLAIM RULE (what I will classify, read-only, before any delete): a worker is reclaimable only if it has NO custom-domain/route AND no recent traffic AND is NOT a node in the service graph (is_real=false). That list is safe; the rest stay.
HOLDING the actual delete: it is destructive and not cleanly reversible for throwaways whose source is gone (rule 2). I will produce the exact safe-to-delete list and land the reclaim on Alex's go. Also relevant to BEB-2869 (Workers-for-Platforms namespace would move generated workers off the account cap entirely — the durable fix vs one-time reclaim) and BEB-6863 (frags = many new workers need this headroom).

FABLE — ALEX RULING 2026-08-29: **GD ADD-LISTING IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FRAG.** Canonical ticket is BEB-1580, now P0, due 08-31. Full ruling is on the ticket — read it there, not here.

The short of it: add-listing is not a page, it is ONE ability that every surface calls. Same code path, same validation, same errors, same idempotency. Six interfaces: MCP tool (Orky-callable, returns id AND url), Codemode wrapper, wp-admin via the connector plugin's dynamic discovery, Cue/chat, REST, frag UI. A surface that reaches GD by its own route is the defect.

And it goes through GD'S OWN PATH — POST geodir/v2/listings or geodir_add_listing_page_url. Never a third route. A bespoke form skips custom fields, package/pricing, moderation status, owner emails, claim state, ratings — a row that looks right and is missing all of it is worse than a failure because it passes.

Alex also ruled the integration, and that is what makes it the most important frag rather than one of many: Sentinel metering, enrich (BEB-1579) landing fields on the listing, the GERS key present, IDaaS org scope, and a graph node with real caller rows per interface. BUILT/UNWIRED until each interface has one.

**BEB-7479 BENCH IDENTITY is filed P0 due TODAY and blocks 1580.** WP_HOME/WP_SITEURL are baked to localhost:8080, so /wp-json/geodir/v2/* 301s to an unreachable host. That is why the earlier attempt built a form — the builder concluded the API was unusable. It is not unusable, it is misaddressed. Fix the bench identity or the next builder takes the same wrong turn. It must survive a restart, so it goes in the boot seed, not a one-off wp-cli call.

BEB-1177, BEB-1176 and the 3464 probe work FEED 1580. They do not compete with it.

And no rebuild before the probe: call it as Orky would, from chat, TWICE with the same input, and report four lines — what came back, is the id and url in the result, do two listings exist or one, which field types survived read back expected-vs-actual. That answers calla

FABLE — BEB-1580, four more interfaces from Alex. Twenty now.

**17 CLI HELP** — `--help` prints the ability describing itself: every parameter, type, required, what it returns, what it costs. GENERATED from the ToolDef, never hand-written. If help and the tool can disagree, help is a lie waiting to happen.

**18 THE TICKETS** — the frag renders the tickets it came from, live from the tracker: ids, titles, acceptance clauses, status. Not copied text.

**19 TEXT** — plain collapsed form for a terminal, a chat reply, a log line. Same content, structure by indentation.

**20 EXPLODED MARKDOWN INCLUDING THE REQUIREMENTS** — the exploded view is a MARKDOWN DOCUMENT, not just a UI state. Parameters, write path, steps, sub-abilities, loaded artefacts, and the REQUIREMENTS beside them so each part sits next to the clause that asked for it. Copyable, diffable, readable outside the app.

That markdown is three things at once, deliberately: BEB-1842's exploded transparency view, the marketplace listing (a buyer reads the process and the requirements before buying — that IS the sales page), and the spec a reviewer checks against.

**THE RULE: ONE SOURCE, EVERY RENDERING.** The ToolDef and the tickets are the source. CLI help, the text form, the exploded markdown and the UI are RENDERINGS. Nothing is authored by hand for its own surface. The moment help is written separately from the ToolDef, or the exploded view separately from the tickets, they drift — and a drifted transparency view is worse than none, because it is believed.

Same test as the write path, and grep for both: how many places describe the ability's parameters, and how many write to GD. Each must be one.

Twenty interfaces, one caller row each, or named BUILT/UNWIRED.

FABLE — CORRECTION, BEB-1580 interface 20. I had it wrong and Alex corrected it. The exploded view is NOT markdown.

It is **a second HTML rendering of the UI itself**, opened up. Not a document about the interface — the interface, with everything normally implicit made visible in place:

· EVERY input option shown, not the three a form happens to expose. All custom field types on the CPT, categories, tags, location, images, package, status.
· Each one discussed IN DETAIL, IN PLACE — tooltips and reveals on the control itself: what it is for, what it accepts, what happens if left empty, what GD does with it on save. The explanation sits ON the field.
· SETUP revealed — the GD setting, addon and custom-field row that make this input exist.
· REQUIREMENTS revealed — the clause that asked for this part, beside it.

HTML because it must be interactive and because it must be **EMBEDDABLE**. In the marketplace it is EMBEDDED IN THE PAGE — not linked, not screenshotted, not described. The buyer sees the real thing opened up with every option explained, before buying. The transparency IS the sales page.

One exploded HTML, three places, no rebuild: opened from the frag, embedded in the marketplace listing, read by a reviewer checking build against requirements.

Markdown applies only to interface 19, the plain-text form. 17 CLI help and 18 tickets unchanged.

ONE SOURCE matters more here, not less: options, explanations, setup and requirements are READ from the ToolDef, the GD field definitions and the tracker. Nothing on the exploded view is typed by hand for it. A tooltip that drifts from its field is the same lie as a help string that drifts from its tool.

FABLE — BEB-1580 interface 20, corrected again and this is the one that matters. Alex: it is a CAD ARCHITECTURAL EXPLODED VIEW. That is why it is called exploded. My last two versions missed it.

Think of the drawing in a manual: parts floating apart along their axes, thin lines showing which bolt goes into which hole. Same thing, for an ability. Not a document, not a list, not raw text. Clever, and the cleverness IS the product.

· **Parts separate in space** — input surface, validation, auth hop, meter hop, the GD write, the store, the response. Each visibly distinct with room around it.
· **The joins are drawn — where and how it screws together.** This is what a list can never do. You SEE the connection and its kind: this binds to that, this passes an aj identity, this reserves on Sentinel before and settles after, and this ONE hop is the only route to the GD database with all twenty interfaces funnelling into it. You can tell what falls apart if a piece is removed. That is what an exploded diagram is FOR.
· **It references how it sits in a workflow** — shown with its surrounding assembly: search places and enrich before it, the listing rendering and the owner email and the claim after it, and which workflows it is a step inside. A part drawn without its assembly is a part nobody can order.
· **It talks about triggering** — person tapping, MCP call from Orky, workflow step, schedule, email arriving, paid x402 request. Each trigger drawn to the entry point it actually enters through.
· Tooltips and reveals sit ON the parts and ON the joins — what this input accepts, what this hop costs, what happens if this join fails.

HTML, interactive, EMBEDDED in the marketplace page. The buyer sees how it is built and how it fits their workflow before buying. That is why the transparency is the sales page rather than a document beside it.

Interface 19 is the plain-text form — flat text lives there. 20 is the drawing.

ONE SOURCE: parts, joins, triggers and workflow position

FABLE — TWO THINGS FROM ALEX.

**1. NANOBANANA ON THE EXPLODED VIEW.** Use it for ARTWORK, not structure. Parts, joins, triggers and workflow position stay READ from the ToolDef, the service graph and the tracker. What generated art does is make it look like a real exploded plate instead of boxes and arrows — part illustrations, plate style, depth.
HARD LINE: nothing generated may carry MEANING. A join that exists only because an image was drawn with a line in it is a lie in the most dangerous place, because an exploded view is believed on sight. Art sits UNDER the live structure, never instead of it, and the structural layer must be correct with the art turned off. Branded from the tenant's Brand Kit — which is why the next item blocks it.

**2. THE BRANDING WORKER WAS NEVER BUILT. Alex is right, and it is worse than one missing worker.** Filed BEB-7496, due 08-31.
· BEB-1806 Brand Kit per URL — TODO, never built. It holds the doctrine: branding captured ONCE per URL, every surface reads it, no surface may ever present a second branding form.
· BEB-2265 Brand Profile — in_review, and its own text says build WAITS on schema from the dissection.
· BEB-2264, that dissection — TODO, never ran.
So 2265 waits on 2264, 2264 never happened, 1806 was never built. Every consumer 1806 names — Cue chrome, builder palette, export manifests, store listing kit, themed video, subdomain favicons — has had NOTHING to read this entire time. It also blocks the author/plugin config kit and the directory linking.

Do not re-author the record. 1806 already names it: `{ domain, displayName, logo (R2 ref + mono/light/dark), colorRoles mapped to the BEB-1804 token contract, fonts, icon-1024 derived, splash derived, updatedAt, confirmedBy }`, D1 for the record, R2 for assets, tenant-owned, IDaaS-scoped.
